name: Intransitive and transitive (lāzim, mutaʿaddī)
definition: A verb is intransitive (lāzim) when its meaning stays with the doer and takes no direct object, transitive (mutaʿaddī) when it passes to an object.
body: Karuma, 'to be noble', is lāzim; ḍaraba, 'to strike', is mutaʿaddī. An intransitive verb can be made transitive in three ways the ṣarf books list: by the pattern afʿala (karuma, akrama, 'to honour'), by the pattern faʿʿala, or by a particle of jarr (dhahaba bihi, 'he took him away'). The muṭāwaʿa patterns go the other way and make a transitive verb intransitive.

examples.text: akrama, 'he honoured': made transitive by the pattern afʿala.
